bernick-building.html: Built in 1885 at 162 River Street North, the Bernick Building has stood at one of Delano’s busiest corners for more than 140 years. The site’s commercial history began in 1869 with John Borsch’s store and saloon, but after the original wooden building was destroyed by fire in 1885, the Bernick family replaced it with the handsome two-story brick building that remains today. Over the decades, the corner became especially well known for its saloons and taverns, including John Stein’s Corner Saloon and, beginning in 1941, the popular Main Bar. In 1956, the building became home to Delano Municipal Liquor, whose on-sale establishment was famously known as “The Zoo.” After the municipal liquor operation moved in 1983, the building served a variety of businesses and today continues its long commercial life as the home of Crow River Studio—preserving a landmark that has witnessed generations of change in downtown Delano.

John L Stein was the proprietor of The Corner Saloon at the turn of the century.  He is the gentleman in the center of this photo.  Over the years, beginning in 1869, there has most often been a saloon or bar on the corner of River Street and Bridge Avenue.

The first building on the corner of Bridge and River Street was a store built in 1869 by John Borsch. It offered groceries and provisions, and a saloon.

When John Borsch built a new store in 1879 on the corner of Franklin and River Street, he sold his old stand to J.M. Eppler.      

In February of 1885, Henry Inwie, then the owner of the property, exchanged his two corner lots on River Street to Jos. Berneck for eighty acres of land.  August Berneck, the son of Joseph, soon after  began a business in the old Borsch building. However, in July, the building was destroyed by fire.

(from the Delano Eagle, July 2, 1885)
   “At 4 o’clock Monday morning an alarm of fire was sounded from River street and the saloon and dwelling house of August Berneck, on the corner of Bridge and River streets, was found to be in flames.  The firemen appeared promptly and no time was lost in getting a stream on the building, which was burning quite slowly owing to the fact that there was no wind blowing. An accident to the hose hampered the firemen’s work, and prevented them from saving the building. The hose burst in three places, and the delay occasioned and the crippled condition of the apparatus allowed the flames to do their work. The building was totally destroyed. Much of the household furniture was removed without damage. The insurance on the building was with the American Philadelphia Company for $1,000, F. H. Lindsley, agent. Later Joseph Berneck’s loss by the fire was adjusted. He got $850 on the building; there was no insurance on the contents.

The Delano Eagle reported in September of 1885 that the building on the corner of Bridge and River streets was being replaced by a much better structure, which would be an ornament to the corner.​

In 1893, the Eagle reported that Berneck  & Jantos owned and ran a saloon and lunch table on the corner of River and Bridge streets, the same business having been located in Delano for eight years, and right on the same corner. Their place of business was in a fine two-story brick building, 25x50,  and “they constantly had on hand a fine line of wines, beer, cigars, etc.”August Berneck retired from the saloon business in 1894, and Matt Fautsch purchased the property in May of that year.
Ad from the Delano Eagle, September 8, 1898
(Sketch of Delano businesses, December, 1898)

In August of 1899, the paper had this article: “Judging from the numerous changes that take place, in the proprietorship of saloons through the county, there must either be a vast amount of money made at the business or very little. Already three men have “retired” from business since Aug. Berneck sold out, all of them making their fortunes (or losing them) in the “corner saloon.” And in December, the problem continued: “Another man has made his fortune (?) in the saloon on the corner of River and Bridge streets and has retired from business. The license was transferred to his successor at a recent special meeting of the village council.”

The Eagle reported in February of 1906 that J. L. Stein had made a contract with Martin Stralka whereby he secured, for 3 years more, the corner building he then occupied.  John Stein died in October of 1906, and again the building had a new occupant, although Martin Stralka still owned it.

In March of 1900 the Delano Eagle reported that Mr. Matt Herriges had given up the saloon business.
John Stein, the saloon-keeper, had moved out of the Pogreba building into the Matt Fautsch building on the corner of River street and Bridge street.  It appears that Martin Stralka owned the Corner Saloon building, but rented it out. He had the old stairway in the rear of the building occupied by John L. Stein torn down and replaced with a substantial new one in 1904. He also had a new ten foot cement walk put down and several other improvements made.

(from the Delano Eagle, September 2, 1909)
   “The unsightly sign for a tobacco company which disfigures the whole north side of Martin Stralka’s building on the corner of River and Bridge streets is an eyesore and a very regrettable innovation. It gives a cheap appearance to the town, is no benefit to the owner of the property and should be removed at the first opportunity.”

In this picture from the mid-1930’s, the sign on the corner store says “Jack Sprat Food Store.”  Jack moved his business to the brick block building in 1941, and the building on the corner of Bridge and River became the Main Bar.
This ad is from the Delano Eagle, June 11, 1941, the Grand Opening of The Main Bar!
Main Bar on River St.
October 12, 1944 – a Poultry Social at The Main Bar!

The “Mainstreet,” a special 1946 edition of the Eagle, described the Main Bar as one of the northwest’s most beautiful lounges. It was owned at that time by Mrs. Magdalena Rose Ferrier, who purchased it from August Dekarski.  The Main Bar was “a popular rendezvous not only for the people of Delano, but also for those from the wide surrounding area.”
This was the bar in the main section of the building.  The bar also had tables and booths.
In 1956 the building became the home to the Delano municipal liquor store, with the on-sale in the main part, and the off-sale shop in the smaller room on the south side.

The on-sale became known as

“The Zoo.”
The opening of Delano Municipal Liquor brought drastic changes to Delano’s downtown, notably the closing of twelve local bars.

The Municipal moved out in 1983 when the city offices moved to the corner of Bridge and Second street, and the building then had various owners and users.  It currently is the home of Crow River Studio, massage therapy and retail gifts.

millinery.html: At a time when few career opportunities were available to women, millinery offered Delano women a way to build independent businesses and serve the fashionable needs of their community. Among the best known was Rosa “Rosie” Geiger Adler Zabel, who opened her millinery business at about age 19 and operated what became the Zabel Style Shop for more than 50 years. Her shop offered carefully crafted hats decorated with velvet, satin, fur, chiffon, silk, feathers, flowers, ribbons, and other fashionable trims, as well as sewing services for local women. Delano was also home to other women in the millinery trade, including Eva Mulford, Maggie O’Leary, Agnes Fleming Leonard, and Bertha Belt. Their shops provided Delano women with the latest styles while giving these early businesswomen an important and distinctive place in the city’s commercial history.
Rosa Geiger Adler Zabel “Rosie’s/ The Zabel Style Shop”

Proprietor of Her Own Shop for Over 50 Years

One of the early business people in Delano

Rosa Geiger was born in 1879 on a farm west of Delano. Her father, Jacob, died in 1885, and the family, consisting of her mother Christina, and three older sisters, Mary, Anna, and Lena, remained on the farm with Henry Rittke as their hired man.. Mary married William Kaeppe in 1888, and Anna married Joseph L. Matter in 1892. The 1895 census shows Christina, Lena and Rosa living with Mary and William, but by 1900 Christina and Rosa had moved into Delano, and Rosa, at age 19, had opened her millinery shop. Rosa married Herman Adler in 1905, and had two children: Mildred and Milton. Herman died unexpectedly from heart trouble in 1911. After Herman’s death, Rosa married again, in 1914, to William F. Zabel, a carpenter. Rosa continued her millinery business, and had a shop on River Street next to Rieder's Meat Market. In the 1946 special Edition of the Delano Eagle called “Mainstreet”: it said: “The Zabel Style Shop first opened its doors in Delano during 1897. Continuing through good times and bad, this shop is still doing business on River Street in Delano. Mrs. Zabel is the owner and operator.” Mildred (Adler) Sawatzke recalled in 1976 in the Delano Centennial book that” her mother’s millinery store started as a sewing shop in about 1900. Three sewing machine operators made custom dresses for the local ladies. The business branched into hats made of buckrum or hat wires shaped to the customers’ wishes. Velvet, satin, fur, chiffon, silk, or straw-braid covered the frames. Genuine ostrich plumes, feathers, jewels, buckles, flowers and ribbons provided the ultimate in decoration. The store was known as Rosie’s and provided local ladies with stylish clothing for over fifty years.” Rosa carried on in her business until illness prevented her. Rosa died in 1954, after 55 years as a Delano businesswoman. She is buried in Schroeder’s Cemetery beside her first husband, Herman A. Adler.

There were not very many opportunities for women to have a business in the early days. One area, however, was that of millinery. As early as 1872,

Mrs. Maria Silvers had a building erected on the corner of Railroad and Second, and opened a millinery shop with her daughter, Minerva Mulford. Mrs. Mulford continued in the business for over twenty-one years. Her business was described in the Delano Eagle in 1893 as follows:

“Mrs. M. J. Mulford –is the most fashionable as well as the oldest milliner of the city, having been in Delano 21 years. Hers is one of the most complete stocks in this section of the state and the store (22x60) presents a very pleasing appearance at all times, for she makes it a point to carry all the latest and most fashionable designs in the millinery line. Here we find all the finest wool fabrics in pretty colors and figures and trimmings to match each. Her display is truly wonderful. Ladies’ furnishings goods for dressing and for fancy work, ribbons and ornaments will make your head swim. Holiday goods and novelties, velvets and zephyrs, etc. in profusion.”

But there was more than one millinery shop in Delano. Mrs. A. Larson had a small general store with a millinery department attached south of the railroad track in 1880, and Miss Maggie O’Leary had a dressmaking establishment on south River Street in 1881. In 1884 Mrs. E. J. Swedeback opened a fashionable millinery parlor on River Street, which she carried on for over 9 years.
Miss Agnes Fleming had her millinery shop in the Mulford building in 1905, and Mrs. F. J. (Bertha) Leonard opened a millinery shop in 1905.

And in 1908 Mrs. Bertha Belt opened her shop, which was still going in 1915. This article from the Great Northwest Magazine dated December, 1909, describes her business: “Oh the joy and expectations with which the female inhabitants of Delano hailed the opening of Mrs. Bertha Belt’s millinery store last December. To say the store is the embodiment of neatness and tidiness is unnecessary when one know the proprietor. She handles millinery of the first degree and aids greatly in pleasing the public because of the fact that she has many original ideas that are very striking and artistic and seems to have a peculiar knack of putting up extremely stylish hats at a nominal cost. No matter what one’s station in life, Mrs. Belt always has a hat, or can readily trim one, that will suit the buyer. The presence of such an artistic milliner is an untold, unlimited benefit and convenience to the people of Delano. Mrs. Belt’s geniality and untiring efforts have won for her friends by the score. When once she has been engaged to trim a hat, it is so satisfactorily doe in every detail that it means a come-back the following season.”

Although the general stores carried women’s clothing and accessories, these business were owned and run by women for women.

rieder-meat-market.html: For generations, Rieder Meat Market was a beloved fixture of downtown Delano and one of the community’s longest-running family businesses. The site at 150 River Street North had housed a meat market since 1876, and in 1911 Leonard J. Rieder and August Schilling established Rieder & Schilling Meat Market. The present building was constructed in 1920, and after Schilling’s death, the business continued through generations of the Rieder family, becoming known for quality meats, personal service, and strong ties to the community. Both Leonard J. Rieder and his son Laurence served as mayors of Delano, further connecting the family to the city’s history. After 115 years under the Rieder name, the market closed in July 2026 with the retirement of third-generation owner Laurence “Bud” Rieder Jr., bringing to a close a remarkable chapter in Delano’s downtown history.
The Rieder Meat Market was the oldest operating business in downtown Delano.

• 1876 1st Building built by S. H. Dyers as a meat market.

  • 1897 Bought by Frank Speckel & John Schaust continued as a meat market

  • 1901 Building purchased by Herman Adler (Adler's Meat Market) from Speckel & Schaust
In 1911 the business was purchased by Leonard J. Rieder & August Schilling (Rieder & Schilling Meat Market). Schilling bought cattle and L.J. ran the meat market.

• 1920 2nd Building constructed.

  • 1946 Schilling died and L.J. Rieder became the sole owner.
1947-1956 Rieder Brothers was run by L.J. 's two sons: Lawrence senior (Bud) & Leonard (who died in 1956)
The present building was constructed in 1920. Active in local politics: both L.J. (Leonard John) and his son Laurence served as Mayors of Delano.

• 1976: Bud Rieder's son, Laurence Jr., took over the business after his father was killed in a car accident.

  • 2019: Betty Rieder, Bud's widow, Betty was still doing the bookkeeping at 92 years old!
The Meat Market close July 4, 2026 when Bud Jr. retired.

plattner-building.html: Since 1892, this building has housed a variety of businesses that reflect Delano’s changing commercial life. It began as John B. Plattner’s General Store, where customers could purchase everything from dry goods and overcoats to boots, hats, furnishings, and notions, promoted through Plattner’s enthusiastic weekly advertisements in the Delano Eagle. In 1913, the building was sold to William Picus, who operated the business until 1920, while Dr. Charles Parker maintained his dental office upstairs. By 1940, Warhol’s Rexall Drug Store occupied the building and featured an impressive 30-foot soda fountain made of Central American primavera wood. The building later became home to Brown Plumbing, and in 1987 began another chapter as Dave’s Town Club, continuing nearly a century of service as a familiar part of Delano’s downtown business district.

J. B. Plattner opened a general merchandise store in Delano in 1892. Then in 1895 he purchased the Steffes building on River Street and moved his goods into what became known as the Plattner building.
“I’m doing business with you because I have just exactly what you want and my prices are simply irresistible.”

It was described as one of the best locations in the village. The whole of the first floor and basement was required to accommodate “one of the largest and most varied assortments of general merchandise in town.” His policy was “one price only, and that price right.” Plattner offered a complete line of dry goods, clothing, hats, caps, shoes, groceries and a five and ten cent department.
Wm Picus bought the business in 1913 and stayed there until about 1918.
Dr. A. E. Phillips had his office above Plattner’s, as did Charles E. Parker, Dentist.
Harold Henk opened a drug store the Plattner building in 1927 and put a new front on the store in 1934.
It featured a 30 foot soda fountain bar made of primavera wood, from Central America.

When there was a fire in the Delano Theater 1937, Katherine Gnitka, living in one of apartments above the Henk Drug Store next to the theater, awoke to heavy smoke pouring into the building and raised the alarm. Damage to the Plattner building was primarily from smoke and water. The Henk Drug Store was succeeded by Warhol Drugs in 1944, and then Moran Rexall Drugs. The next resident was Brown Bros. Plumbing, who were in the building when the theater again has a fire in 1971, this time destroying it completely.

Dave Carroll bought the building in 1992, which had been vacant for twenty years, He spent 4 ½ months renovating the interior and opened November 10, 1992. Dave’s Town Club is still there today (2026).
“Tippy’s Town Tavern” next to Dave’s Town Club during the filming of the movie “A Simple Plan’” in 1998.
The sign on the side of Dave’s Town Club is from the movie.

120-river-st-n.html: Built around 1897, the building at 120 River Street North has served a remarkable variety of Delano businesses for more than a century. One of its earliest occupants was a confectionery, followed by a jewelry store by 1909; in 1925, watchmaker and jeweler Peter Magdzas purchased the business, and Peter’s Jewelry remained there for sixteen years. In 1941, Don Bartlett and Ray Kiefer purchased the building and moved their popular tavern there, followed by Shelly and Sterling Robson, who operated the bar until Delano established its Municipal Liquor Store in 1956. The building later housed the Delano Chiropractic Office, the Perkins and Grinley Law Office, and optometrist Dr. Dale R. Petersen. Continuing its long history as a downtown business location, Delano Floral & Gifts has occupied the building since 2014.
Built in approximately 1897, one of the first businesses in it was a confectionary.

There was a jewelry store in the building as early as 1909, as shown on the Sanborn maps. In 1925 Peter Magdzas, watchmaker and jeweler, bought the store and business from T.C. Jones. Peter’s Jewelry remained there for sixteen years.

In 1941 Don Bartlett and Ray Keifer, who had been in business together since 1932, bought the building from Magdzas and moved their tavern there from across the street. It was described as one of the finest taverns in the state. Bartlett and Kiefer were both hospitable and efficient and had many friends and customers in the vicinity.

Shelly and Sterling Robson had the bar after Barlett & Kiefer. They were there from 1952, until 1956, when the Municipal Liquor Store was approved, and all other liquor licenses in Delano were eliminated.
The Delano Chiropractic Office opened in the Sterling building.
The Perkins and Grinley Law Office was in the building in the 1970’s, and Dr. Dale R. Petersen, Optometrist.
Delano Floral & Gifts has been in the building since 2014.

borsch-building.html: Built in 1897 at 116 River Street North, the John E. Borsch Building has housed more than a century of Delano businesses, beginning with T. B. Rader’s hardware and well supplies and later A. W. Wittman’s drug store. In 1921, Edward W. Keplinger purchased the building and moved his grocery business there, eventually opening Delano’s first Red & White store. After his death, his son Horace “Kep” Keplinger and wife Esther continued the business, expanding its produce operation—especially eggs—into an enterprise that eventually grew into Wrightco. Although the building was gutted by fire in 1932, it was rebuilt and continued serving Delano through a succession of businesses. Today, the historic storefront is home to Mainstreet Boutique, continuing the building’s long tradition as part of Delano’s River Street business district.
In 1897 John E. Borsch erected a solid brick store building, 25x85 feet, north of John Coolen’s Hardware store.

T. B. Rader had his hardware and well supplies business in the building in 1898, and A.W. Wittman moved his drug store from Railroad Avenue to the John E. Borsch building in 1908. He remained there until 1921.

In February of 1920, Edward W. Keplinger and his son-in-law William Tarzwell moved with their families from Wisconsin to Delano. They bought the Delano Café, located on Bridge Avenue in the Brick Block building, from C. M. Peterson and took over the business.
Newell Kidder, E. W. Keplinger, Evelyn (Keplinger) Tarzwell, William Tarzwell, holding Irene Tarzwell, Joyce Keplinger, Goldie Keplinger, Francis Plotnik, Basil Tarzwell (standing in front)

In April of 1921 Keplinger bought the John E. Borsch building on River Street, and soon after moved the store there. He opened the first Red & White store in 1927, advertising the benefits of having the buying power of an international chain store system.

E.W. died in 1930, and his son Horace E. “Kep” Keplinger dropped out of college to succeed his father in operating the business, going into partnership with his mother in what was then known as Keplinger’s Grocery and Produce. Due to the depression, farmers were paying for their groceries with produce such as cream, poultry, and eggs.

In 1932 the store was gutted by fire. Horace E. Keplinger rebuilt the store, adding the produce department. That end of the business had phenomenal growth, especially with eggs, soon outstripping the original business in importance.
The Keplinger Food Store in Delano, located on River Street.
Interior of the store as pictured in the 1946 “Main Street”
The building was used by several different businesses over the ensuing years, alternating with being vacant.
In 2026, the building is the home of Mainstream Boutique, “a women’s clothing boutique” that is intentionally multi-generational.

post-office.html: Delano’s postal history began in 1858 with the Cassel post office west of present-day Delano. With the arrival of the railroad in 1868, postal service shifted to the new community along the Crow River, which soon took the name Delano in honor of railroad official Francis Roach Delano. Over the following century, the post office moved among several downtown businesses and buildings and was served by a long succession of postmasters, including Delano’s first female postmaster, Miranda Chance, in 1880. Rural free delivery began in 1901, with three routes eventually serving Delano and surrounding communities. In 1926, the post office moved into the former First National Bank building on River Street, where it remained until a new post office was built and dedicated in 1965—the same year Delano experienced its record-breaking flood. The story continues through generations of postmasters and changing postal services, reflecting more than 165 years of Delano’s growth and community life.

The first post office was established in 1858 in the area was west of present Delano and was named Cassel. The first postmaster was Theodore Jaegler. He was succeeded by William Ziebarth in 1865, John Tuckson in 1966, and David White in 1867. Soon after the coming of the railroad in 1868, the Cassel office was discontinued, and the Crow River office was established. Sometimes, in those early days, whenever any settlers went to St. Anthony Falls for supplies, they brought back mail addressed to (name), Minneapolis, Minnesota – Crow River. It was then left at William Wasson’s small store, which was in J. P. Lyle’s old log house. Delano’s first postmaster was Frank M. Hopkins. Appointed in December 1868, his office was in his general store across from the depot. It was found that there was a Crow River post office already in Minnesota as well as other names that were considered. Finally, a meeting was held on the depot platform, and it was decided to name the post office Delano, after Francis Roach Delano, a railroad official. In the winter of 1868-69 Frank B. Nichols built a general store and was the second postmaster, appointed in 1871.

J. M. Langford was appointed postmaster in 1872; his assistant was Miss Kerr. Again, the office was in a different location. Mrs. Miranda Chance was Delano’s first female postmaster, appointed in 1880; the office was in the Chance drug store. Her assistant was her son, Norman Chance, who was appointed postmaster in 1883. Valentine Eppel was the next postmaster; the post office was located on Main Street. Charles H. Vorse was appointed next, with the office remaining in the same building. Michael O’Hair was appointed in 1893; he moved the post office back to where Mrs. Chance had it. Frank C. Lindsley became the postmaster in 1897, moving the office into his own building on Second Street. Clarence J. Buckley, first appointed in 1903 and serving for three terms began in the Lindsley building, moved down the street, and finally used the former Wright County Bank building as the post office.

“The post office has been moved to the building recently occupied by the Wright County Bank, and it is expected that the new quarters will prove very convenient and desirable. The building is one of the best structures in town and there is ample accommodation for the R.F.D. carriers in the large room back of the main office.” (from the Delano Eagle, January 21, 1909)

Henry Bock was next appointed in 1916, serving two terms. He started out in the former back building, later moving to his own building in the brick block on Bridge Avenue. Miss Elizabeth Richardson, who worked as the assistant to both C. J. Buckley and Henry Block, was appointed postmaster in 1925. The post office was moved into the former First National Bank building on River Street August 26, 1926, (The building occupied by LuLu’s Retail Therapy In 2025.) Albert O. McEachern became postmaster in 1933, and served 31 years, retiring in 1964. Wally Grotz was appointed in 1965 and was in charge of the post office during the record-breaking flood of that year.
He was also the postmaster when the new post office was built and dedicated in 1965.

Paul E. Naegeli was appointed postmaster in 1982, followed by Howard A. Leathers in 1993, Josephine Ambroz in 1996, Darryl W. Peterson in 1999, and Dale R. Gatz in 2000. In 2005 Larry D. Matson became Delano’s postmaster. Debra R. Eriech served starting in 2012, and in 2014 Mark P. Hayes was appointed and remains Delano’s postmaster in 2026.

Mr. ZIP, the mascot for the U.S. Postal Service's Zone Improvement Plan (ZIP Code), was officially unveiled to the public at a convention of postmasters in October 1962. The five-digit ZIP Code system itself was introduced on July 1, 1963.

Rural free delivery was started in Delano in March, 1901. Route No. 1 was established with D. L. Sutton (Roy) as carrier. His salary was $600 including horse hire. On October 1st of the same year two more routes were established: R. E. Brunkow becoming carrier for Route No. 2, and Otto L. Kelsey for No. 3. The following year Brunkow resigned, and Peter Beissel took his place.

About 1909 or 1910 Wm. Sutton succeeded his brother Roy as carrier for No. 1. These three carriers from the Delano office served people near Watertown, Rockford, Montrose and Lyndale, besides the Delano community.

Rural residents were required to display signals on their mailboxes when they left mail in them for carriers to collect as of July 1, 1906. Carriers had to lower the signals on boxes after making collections, providing no mail was left, and had to display the signal when they had deposited mail for the resident.

delano-lions.html: The Delano Lions Club supports the community through local events, fundraising, and infrastructure projects. The Lions Club was organized in Delano in November 1965 with twenty-one members on the original list and several more joining by the charter night, December 9, 1965. The Lions Club was organized to fill the need in Delano for a service club. The organizing members felt that they could contribute to the overall improvement of the Delano community. Over the next several years the Lions sponsored Cub Scouts, bike safety clinics, Tots-to-Teens Talent contests, the Lions Eye Bank, the Christmas lighting contest, and snowmobile races. They furnished playground equipment and a shelter in Central Park, and became instrumental in the 4th of July celebration. The Lions purchased a Rescue truck for the Delano Fire Department and were involved in having Delano join the Great River Regional library system, and in financing the renovation of the library. The Lions built the entryway to the Franklin Township Hall and were founding members of the original Delano Community Development Committee that brought Industrial Louvers (then ACP) to Delano.

In 1966 they sponsored the Innertube Derby as part of Delano’s 4th of July celebration. The race went from the half-way bridge on the Crow River to Bridge Street in Delano. The winner was Dave Zitzloff, Carl Johannsen was second, and Jim Stahlke came in third.
In 1977 the Lions developed a new hockey rink on Delano Park property near the waste water treatment plant and turned it over to the city.

The Delano Lions are currently active hosting Christmas trees sells and doing a neighborhood tree pickup after the holidays. They continue to collect used eyeglasses and hearing aids. Delano Lions recruit, organize and facilitate Delano’s 4th of July parade, Minnesota’s largest and longest. And they sponsor the BBQ Rib Fest.

delano-boy-scouts-troop-273.html:
Boy Scouts of America got its start in 1910. Eight years later, Delano welcomed Troop 273 (formerly 173). For nearly 100 years, hundreds of scouts from Delano and the surrounding communities have worked to better themselves by giving back their community.

In the Fall of 1928, nine young Delano boys started blazing a trail for decades of scouts to follow. Whether it was learning valuable outdoor skills, learning how to be a good citizen, or serving their community;

Delano Scouts continue to serve our city with pride..

During times of war and times of peace, Delano Scouts have stood the test of time and remains a strong and active community organization. Delano Scouts are involved in supporting community events including Old Fashioned Christmas, collecting food for the Delano Food Shelf, 4th of July Celebrations and much more.

The troop meets most Mondays at the Heritage Center

delano-loretto-girl-scouts.html: Girl Scouting in Delano began in the summer of 1931, less than 20 years after the national organization was founded. Early Girl Scouts participated in camping, swimming, canoeing, outdoor cooking, crafts, nature study, community activities and local fundraising. Delano Girl Scouts History After the original troop became inactive, Girl Scouting was reorganized in Delano in 1951 with 29 girls and grew to include Brownie and Intermediate troops. A major change came in 1965 when Delano joined the Greater Minneapolis Girl Scout Council and organized Brownie, Junior, Cadette and Senior levels. Delano Girl Scouts History Generations of local women have served as scouts and leaders, including Maria Logsdon, who contributed at least 20 years of service. Eventually known as the Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts, the organization has carried forward a tradition of friendship, leadership, service and outdoor adventure that began in Delano in 1931. Delano Girl Scouts History Delano Girl Scouts History

The first Girl Scout troop in Delano was organized in the summer of 1931, less than 20 years after Girl Scouting began nationally in 1912. The first Delano leaders were Mrs. Charles Parker and Mrs. Bert Gilmer. In 1934, Mrs. Paul Kruell joined as an assistant leader.

Girl Scouts at Girl Scouts in camp uniforms washing up at Camp Greenwood, Buffalo, Minnesota in 1938. Camp Greenwood is the camp Delano Girl Scouts would attend yearly.

The early Delano troop apparently operated throughout the year. Activities included swimming, canoeing, outdoor cooking in both winter and summer, Christmas caroling, crafts, nature study, and taffy pulls. The girls also raised money locally: they held an Easter sale and sold Easter eggs, and during Delano's Fourth of July celebration they sold ice cream bars.

That original troop eventually became inactive.

Girl Scouting was reorganized in Delano in 1951, with 29 girls participating. The leaders named in the historical account were:

Mrs. Harold Petersen

Mrs. Mary Trueman

Mrs. Art Russek

Mrs. Charles King

The new troop continued many of the same traditional scouting activities as the 1930s group. As participation increased, Delano developed both Brownie and Intermediate Girl Scout troops. Girls also attended Girl Scout camp at Nest Lake, with cookie sales helping pay many of the camping fees.

A particularly important date is 1965. Until then, Delano's Girl Scouts had apparently operated as a "lone troop," rather than as part of a larger Girl Scout council.

In 1965, Delano joined the Greater Minneapolis Girl Scout Council. The local program was reorganized into the Girl Scout age levels then in use: Brownies, Juniors, Cadettes and Seniors. A Cadette troop was established in Delano in 1966.

The surviving account shows substantial growth after that transition. At the time the history was written, Delano had:

Brownie - 29 - Lead by Mrs. Joe Martin, Mrs. Bill Loomis, Mrs. Arndt, Mrs. Nee

Juniors - 41 - Lead by Mrs. Milton Voltin, Mrs. Dale Barth

Cadette - Seniors — Mrs. Ronald Habstritt
Maria Logsdon — at least 20 years of service

One name especially stands out: Maria Logsdon.

The historical account says Mrs. Logsdon had completed 20 years helping Delano Girl Scouts. She served as a Brownie, Junior and Cadette leader and later represented the Delano-Loretto Service Unit as both a Girl Scout Council delegate and Community Association delegate.

There is also evidence of former Delano Girl Scouts becoming leaders themselves. The history specifically mentions Mary Wandersee (Mrs. Michael DeWitte) and Lynn Rieland (Mrs. Gary McClay) as former scouts who later served as leader and assistant with Cadette troops.

Eventually the organization became identified as the Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts/Service Unit. This wasn't merely an old name: a Girl Scouts River Valleys service-unit map from 2020 still identifies Delano/Loretto as Service Unit 136.

Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts at Camp Elk River on March 11, 2017. The encampment was hosted by the Cadette Troop. The Cadette Troop planned all the activities, food and entertainment for a Friday night to Sunday afternoon encampment.

Delano-Loretto Girl Scouts have had active membership dating back to when the first Girl Scout Troops started in Delano in 1931.

To learn more about Girl Scout and join a Troop visit. https://www.girlscoutsrv.org/

stein-barber-shop.html: The Stein family’s barbering legacy in Delano began with Armand Stein, who started at the Bock Barber Shop in 1912 at just eight years old, shining shoes and lathering customers for shaves. Licensed as a barber at only 15, Armand later traveled to California, where he cut the hair of several Hollywood actors before returning to Delano and opening Stein’s Barber Shop in 1932. Armand retired in 1978 after 61 years of barbering, while his son Fran, who joined him in 1967, continued the family tradition. When the historic River Street building was demolished by controlled burn in 2006, Fran moved the shop to Bridge Avenue, preserving its original backbar, 1917 barber chairs, and rare hand-cranked barber pole. He continued barbering until selling the shop in 2025. Together, Armand and Fran Stein provided Delano with an extraordinary 119 years of barbering service spanning two generations.

Armand Stein

Armand was the youngest son of John Louis Stein, an early saloonist in Delano and one of the builders of the Brick Block Building on Bridge Street. Armand started working in the Bock barber shop in 1912. He was eight years old and started off by shining shoes and lathering faces for shaves.
August Bock, Hamilton, Charlie and Fred Bock, Armand Stein (in chair), Carl “Rooster” Eckman, Eddie Bock.

During World War I, there was a shortage of barbers in Delano, because many the barbers went to work in defense plants for the war effort. Armand’s brother-in-law, Charlie Bock, took him to the governor, and the governor granted the 15-year-old his license.

In 1922, Armand headed to Seattle with his barber equipment, eventually going to Los Angeles, and then Hollywood. The Delano Eagle reported in 1925 that Armand was very enthusiastic about California. He cut the hair of several celebrities, including Hoot Gibson, Thomas Meighan, William Boyd (better known as Hopalong Cassidy) and many other well known actors. But in 1926 Armand returned to Delano, working for various barbers. In 1932 he opened his own shop, known for years as Stein’s Barber Shop.
Stein Barber Shop on left; Bartlett & Kiefer Bar on right
Armand Stein and Carl Eckman in Stein’s Barber Shop, 1946

Fran Stein

Armand’s son, Fran Stein, began working with him in Stein’s Barber Shop in 1967 after graduating from barber school. He barbered out of the same shop for 39 years.

Stein’s Barber Shop on River Street was in a building built in 1880. It was originally a hook and ladder company. The north part of the building was added in 1917. In the 1920’s and early 1930’s it was known as Peschek’s Hardware building. Bartlett and Kiefer’s Tavern was in the building until 1941, when A.J. Boyce bought it to house the Boyce Funeral Parlor. Other businesses that were in the building over the years included a television and repair shop, a sports shop, Art Russek’s propane gas shop, and the Putkammer Insurance Agency and Intercom Technology.
In 2006 Stein’s Barber Shop building on River Street, suffering from both foundation and roof problems, was burned down in a controlled burn.

Fran moved to 203 Bridge Ave., across the street from the Delano City Hall, taking history with him in the form of the backbar, chairs bought new in 1917, and the hand-cranked barber pole, of which there are only one or two of that type left in the country. Fran continued in the new location for nearly twenty more years, selling the shop in 2025. Armand barbered for 61 years, Fran for 58 years. Between the two of them, Delano was fortunate to have 119 years of barbering by the Steins.

dacac.html: The mission of the Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture is to empower people to think, work and live creatively through arts and cultural experiences.
The purpose is to promote collaboration and provide support to other community arts and cultural organizations. Provide art and cultural events for all ages.
Delano Old-Fashioned Christmas
2019: Delano Old-Fashioned Christmas - Storybook Characters The Arts Council's started this annual festival in 2009.
Delano Sculpture Park

“Flood of ’65” Sculpture by International sculptor, Zoran Mojsilov. Historical artifacts were donated by the Delano Middle School 8th grade art class and the community in 2011-12. Can be seen in the Delano Sculpture Park on Hwy 12. The Arts Council worked with the city to create a Public Art Policy. The Sculpture Park has expanded to hold multiple permanent sculptures and annual sculptures that are displayed for a year, available for purchase and are replaced the following year.
4th of July Street Art
2019: 4th of July Street Art Contest: Guest Artist Shawn McCann, sponsored by Delano Public Library. The first Street Art Contest was held 2017.

2015-18: The Arts Council worked with the Delano Labyrinth Committee. The labyrinth is an interactive public art project that offers an oasis of calm in a busy world. Located in the Highway 12 Sculpture Park.
Spirit of Community Trail
2019: Debbie DeBeer and Sarah Hellmich lead a guided walking tour of the Delano Heritage Trail.
The Heritage Trail expanded to the Spirit of Community Trail, a comprehensive history of many of the buildings, businesses and organization that made and make Delano the city it is today.
Rieder Homestead Concerts

Rieder Homestead Concerts is a music series that began in 2016 in the Historic Rieder Homestead Barn on Bridge Avenue in Delano.  Dave Dennison, a neighbor of the Rieder’s and a video producer, started the concerts after using the building as a “set” for a series of music videos. After seeing owner Dave Rieder and his son Logan watch the video production, he was struck by their wonder at the musicians’ talents. After discussing the idea of holding concerts in the 1881 barn, Dennison and Rieder hosted their first in May 2016.  Soon after, they began hosting outdoor concerts on a homemade stage.  More than 200 concerts later, Rieder Homestead Concerts has built a national reputation for quality concerts featuring orginal songwriters from all over the United States, Canada, and the UK.  Shows are by reservation only, drawn from a private email list. To join, email riederhomesteadconcerts@gmail.com.
Delano Community Band

The Delano Community Band is an inter-generational ensemble proudly based in Delano, Minnesota. Since 2017, we've united musicians from all walks of life—from enthusiastic high school students to accomplished performers with decades of experience. This dynamic mix fosters both musical excellence and meaningful connections, offering a rewarding opportunity for growth, collaboration, and community celebration through music.
Directed by Mike Dailey

The Delano Community Band, commissioned Randall Standridge to write the musical piece titled ‘Unbound Celebrations’

The composition was first played at the Delano Sesquicentennial Jamboree, October 3, 2026, in celebration of Delano's Sesquicentennial and dedicated to the people of Delano, whose community spirit has shaped the city's first 150 years.
Delano Dramatic Company

The current version os Delano Dramatic Company (DDC) was newly formed in 2022, when some key people who have deep roots in the Delano Public Schools drama program and community theatre came together with input from others in our community to form a new theatre company in Delano. The concept for this new company was also supported by the Delano Schools, the Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture - which served as the fiscal agent for the group in its inaugural year - the Delano Area Community Foundation, and local civic groups.

The genesis of the name for Delano Dramatic Company had its roots in Delano history. The City's own website notes this history: "In September 1890, work began to build a stage upstairs in the [city] hall so theatrical performances could be held. The next year the village purchased stage scenery to equip the stage. A year later dressing rooms were added on each side of the stage. Also, in 1890 the Delano Dramatic Company offered to pay $100 toward $250 needed for a piano... "

DDC offers adjunct theatrical opportunities in the Delano area, where interested community members of all ages and backgrounds can participate. The drama programs offered to students from elementary age through high school within Delano Public Schools are excellent and have strong student participation. These programs are well supported by district staff and by the community, both as audience members and as volunteers.

Businesses and organizations in the community also provide strong support through financial sponsorships, advertising, and the like. The school district itself has supported DDC's work by making audition, rehearsal and performance spaces available for our large scale summer musicals. Local churches and the City's senior center have welcomed DDC's more intimate performances of dramatic and comedic plays.

Since 2022, DDC has produced four Broadway musicals on the Delano Performing Arts Center (PAC) stage, and four smaller plays in area churches and the senior center. Many talented adults and youth from Delano have participated in these eight productions: "Christmas with a Twist", "School of Rock", "Jacob Marley's Christmas Carol", "Sound of Music", "Grace and Glorie", "Billy Elliot the Musical" "Tuesdays with Morrie" and Disney's "Newsies".

DDC also supports other community events like the Delano 4th of July activities; the Olde Fashioned Christmas celebration, and the Delano Sesquicentennial by providing actors, staging and costumes. We also support the school drama programs by donating production elements, such as scenery, props and costumes, and allowing high school drama boosters to sell candygrams at performances as a fundraiser.

In the four and a half years of our existence, we have become a valuable, integral part of the arts community of Delano. Our president also represents DDC on the Delano Area Council for Arts and Council.

Delano’s Sesquicentennial Tribute

For the Sesquicentennial the Arts Council worked on three comprehensive projects. Starting in 2024 they commissioned a public sculpture called ‘Sesquicentennial’ by James and Ryan Pedersen.

They also created a Community Tile Project where people of all ages decorated a ceramic tiles with permanent markers. The tiles were photographed and the participant took their tile home. The photos were embedded into photos of four of LeAnna Wurzer’s paintings, depicting Delano, The Crow River and the Indigenous that came before, the Agriculture, Railroad, and Industry. This became a mosaic that was installed on the retaining wall for the Sesquicentennial Sculpture.

To help support these project the council sold Heritage Bricks, dedicated to individuals, families, business, and organizations. The bricks were laid in front of the mosaic, creating a tribute to Delano’s 150 years.
Grants from the Central Minnesota Arts Board, Legacy Funds and Delano Area Foundation have helped make the Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture bring Art and Culture to Delano
